Subject: Re: Aurora DPA questions — draft responses

Hi all —

Thanks for the workbook, Jasmine. I reviewed with Infra/Legal and drafted a short DPA response doc (attached as redwood-dpa-draft-2027.pdf). High-level responses below — happy to go into detail on any item during a sync:

- Controller/Processor: Aurora is Controller; Redwood will be Processor for processing under the proposed contract. We do not expect any joint-controller relationship for standard usage patterns (we flagged joint-controller language only if Aurora requires model-derivative usage tied to product analytics).

- Subprocessors: we maintain a current subprocessor list and will provide it to Aurora. Our standard commitment: 30 days’ notice prior to onboarding a new subprocessor, plus the right for customers to object on reasonable privacy/security grounds; for urgent security-critical subprocessors we provide notice as soon as practicable. We can include this for Aurora in the DPA.

- Breach notice: our contractual maximum notification window is 72 hours for confirmed data breaches affecting customer PII. For incidents requiring forensic work, we provide an initial notification within 72 hours and follow-up updates as we learn more. We can include regular reporting cadence in the DPA.

- Data residency & transfers: Redwood hosts customer data in region-appropriate cloud regions. For Aurora (US customers), we can commit to US-region processing and storage for PII under the Dedicated/Private deployment option. For Hosted API customers we rely on region config and contractual commitments; we will document cross-border transfer mechanisms (SCCs/other) in the DPA.

- Retention & logs: default request/response logs are retained for 90 days; KV cache entries and embeddings are retained according to configured workspace defaults (90 days) but can be set to shorter windows by agreement. We can offer a contractual option to reduce retention to 30 days for request logs and embeddings subject to technical feasibility and pricing impact.

Rishi, can you confirm the current default windows and any operational constraints for offering 30-day retention for embeddings? Also attaching a suggested clause for breach notice and subprocessor notification.

If Aurora is comfortable with this language, we can produce a redline for the DPA and route for signature. Happy to join a 30-min legal sync — Marissa, I’m available 10:00–12:00 PDT on May 6.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Legal Counsel | Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.ai

Attachment: redwood-dpa-draft-2027.pdf

Hi Jasmine —

Thanks for sending these — looping in our legal and infra teams with proposed responses attached (redwood-dpa-draft-2027.pdf). Quick summary of what we can commit to contractually:

- Role: Aurora = Controller, Redwood = Processor (standard usage).
- Subprocessors: we will provide a current subprocessor list within 24 hours and commit to 30 days’ notice for new subprocessors with exception process for urgent security needs.
- Breach notice: initial notification within 72 hours for confirmed incidents affecting PII; follow-up updates and forensic support as available.
- Data residency: for US customer PII we can commit to US-region processing/storage for Dedicated or Private deployments; hosted options will be documented with transfer mechanisms (SCCs) if cross-border transfer is needed.
- Retention: default 90 days for request logs, KV cache and embeddings; we can offer 30-day retention as an option (implementation and pricing impact to be confirmed by infra).

Next steps:
1) Please confirm which of the above items require redline language vs. acceptance of proposed wording.
2) If you’d like a contract redline, we’ll prepare and share the DPA redline by EOD May 7.
3) We can run a 30-min legal sync on May 6 at 10:30 AM PDT if that works for your team (Neha and Rishi will join).

Also including a link to our SOC 2 report and a HubSpot deal for tracking: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/1234567/deal/RDW-2027-0892.

If that timeline works I’ll get the redline started.
